item: Deeper study — the devout daily reader (deeper_study)
angle: Behavioural habit design: the unit of reading, the trigger, the reward, the grace, the identity language, the return visit.
thesis: This reader does not need motivating. They already read five days a week for ten minutes, and the app is currently measuring the wrong thing, showing them the same chapter twice, giving them an AI paragraph where six real commentaries are already installed, and letting them fall silently behind a dated plan with no way back. Four fixes, in this order: put the text first and the depth one tap under it in a named row; count the rhythm they actually keep (days read out of the last seven) instead of a perfect chain that resets every Monday for a weekday reader; never let a missed day become a lost passage — offer catch-up before guilt; and make the reminder name their own next chapter. Nothing is removed from the screen. The tools all stay, named, one row lower, so the passage gets the screen and the depth gets a door.
principles: The passage owns the screen. Depth is one tap away, always in the same place, always named — never auto-dumped and never hidden behind an unlabelled icon.

Count weeks kept, not days unbroken. The target behaviour for this persona is 5 days in 7 (research, Persona 3 header), so the counter must be able to say yes to 5 in 7. A perfect-chain streak structurally cannot.

Credit only what they did. A devout reader will notice a counter that lies, and once they stop trusting the number they stop trusting the app. Arrival never credits; expanding never credits; only a deliberate Mark as read or listening to the end credits.
Never let a missed day become a lost passage. Falling behind must be visible, small, and reversible in one tap — that is the grace, and it replaces the streak freeze for this persona.
Identity language, not praise. "You read most days" and "12 weeks running", never "amazing" and never an exclamation mark.
The trigger names their chapter or it is noise. A generic day-of-year verse push to a reader on day 12 of Through the Bible in a Year is an interruption, not a cue.

Richer and clearer, never stripped. Every tool that is on the screen today is still on the screen after this change — Commentary, Compare, Greek and Hebrew are promoted into one visible, named Study row instead of one being force-expanded and two being hidden in the chrome.

journey.day0: They arrive already devout and pick "Deep Bible study" from the one sheet (ChoosePathSheet, unchanged — one tap saves and opens, ruling). Home opens on a reading straight away (arrival seed, credit-free, unchanged). Below the reading, where plan_scripture renders nothing today because there is no active plan, a three-card plan chooser: Through the Bible in a Year, The New Testament in 90 days, Psalms and Proverbs, plus "See all plans". Three, not twenty-two — research: "choose a plan, two or three at most". The card footer carries the promise that decides whether they start: "Miss a day and the reading waits for you." Tapping a plan starts it dated from today and Home re-seeds to day 1. Nothing else is asked. No streak is mentioned on day 0.
journey.first_session: Greeting, plan line, the chapter already open in the white paper panel. They read. Under the last verse: the Study row (Commentary · Compare · Greek & Hebrew), then the Reflect box, then Mark as read. Tapping Commentary opens the Study drawer with real named commentaries from the study library (Matthew Henry, Jamieson Fausset & Brown, Calvin, Keil & Delitzsch, Gill, Clarke) rather than the ~20-chapter curated set plus an AI paragraph. They tap Mark as read. The done moment says "Day done." and "Day 1 of 365." — no streak number on day one, because a 1 is a worse cue than nothing.
journey.return_visit: Same shape every day: greeting, rhythm line, plan line, chapter open, Study row, Reflect, Mark as read. The rhythm line is the only thing that changes and it changes gently: "5 of the last 7 days." From four qualifying weeks on it adds the identity clause: "5 of the last 7 days. 12 weeks running." Because the count is a rolling seven-day window and not a chain, a Saturday and Sunday off never zeroes it — it reads 5, which is exactly what they did.
journey.week2: By day 8–14 on a 365-day plan the reader has almost certainly missed one or two days (research: busyness is the #1 reason reading declines, 40–58%). Today the missed passage silently disappears — calcPlanDay is calendar-elapsed, so day 12 shows day 12 and days 9–11 are gone from Home forever. From week 2 they instead see a small banner above the reading: "3 readings waiting", the chapter names, "Read Genesis 9" and "Move the plan to today". Whichever they choose, they end the session level. This is the single highest-leverage moment in the whole two weeks and it is currently unhandled.
journey.missed_day: Nothing is said on the day itself. On return: the rhythm line drops honestly ("3 of the last 7 days.") with no apology and no repair theatre; the catch-up banner names what is waiting; the reminder that evening names the waiting chapters rather than the streak. After a longer gap (nothing in the last 7 days) the greeting acknowledges the record instead of greeting a long-time reader like a first-timer: "Welcome back. Your longest run is 46 days. It starts the same way." — the existing streak_reset_best line (i18n.ts:425) re-pointed at the rhythm data. No guilt copy anywhere, ever; guilt-framed streak reminders drive notification opt-out and uninstall (research, cross-cutting #6).
journey.seasonal: One moment in this persona's first year, not a programme: from mid-December the plan chooser offers "Start on 1 January" as a second button on the year-long plans, because 1 Jan drives 3M+ one-year-plan starts (research, cross-cutting #5) and a plan started on 18 December is a plan abandoned on 2 January. Everything else seasonal (church-wide reads with a live count) belongs to the cross-cutting design, not this path.

Today the body always names a global ALL_PASSAGES day-of-year rotation, so a reader on day 12 of a year plan is pinged about an unrelated chapter.

comfort_access: One quiet row at the very foot of Home, below the Bible AI row, on every path — for this persona: "Hard day? There is a quieter reading here." It opens today's comfort reading directly and does NOT change dw_setup, so a devout reader can take a gentle day without losing their path, their plan or their rhythm count. This is the cross-cutting "comfort from everywhere" move (research build order #2: one persistent tap, highest duty of care, smallest build), placed where it cannot interrupt: last, muted, never a modal, never a prompt. The existing route also stays — the PathSwatch pill is on every Home for every persona and the sheet's comfort card is one tap from it (ruling: three doors, never a gate). Two things are deliberately not built here: nothing that asks a devout reader whether they are struggling, and nothing resembling a graduation or "feeling stronger" prompt in either direction — that prompt is removed for good and is never to be re-added in any form.
reminders: One push a day at the reader's chosen hour, naming their own next chapter and its length ("Genesis 12 — Day 12 of Through the Bible in a Year. About 10 minutes."), because a generic day-of-year verse is an interruption to someone who knows exactly where they are. When they are behind, the push names the waiting chapters instead. Nothing ever mentions a streak, a loss, or a number at risk — guilt-framed streak reminders drive notification opt-out and uninstall (research, cross-cutting #6), and this is the persona most likely to have a legitimate reason for their two days off. Back-off is explicit: three unopened pushes in a row triggers one "Still here when you are", then weekly until they open the app again, at which point daily resumes. The hour and the on/off switch stay where they are in MoreScreen, with one line added under them stating the contract: "One a day, at the time you pick. Never about a streak." Behaviour-inferred timing (Duolingo's approach, research cross-cutting #6) is the next step after this ships, not part of it — it needs the event data below first. Verification note: pushSupported() only allowlists futuresdailyword.com, www and localhost, so the reminder change cannot be proven on a deploy preview — it is checked on localhost, then on prod after merge.
instrumentation: study_open — fired once per session on Home for deeper_study. Detail: plan id, day number, days_behind, has_read_today. This is the D1/D7/D30 denominator by path, which no public source will ever supply (research build order #1).
study_read_complete — deliberate completion only. Detail: ref, seconds_on_passage, source (button | audio_end | catchup). Replaces the ambiguity of today's daily_reading, which fires on expand.
study_tool_open — detail: commentary | crossrefs | words | compare | greek. Answers the research's named test: Study collapsed vs open on session length and 30-day retention.

study_catchup_shown / study_catchup_read / study_catchup_rebase — the funnel for the grace mechanic. The number that matters is 30-day retention for readers who rebase vs readers who see the banner and do nothing.

study_rhythm_week — fired once per local week. Detail: days_read (0-7), weeks_running. This is the identity metric; it is also the honest measure of whether this persona is retained, in a way a streak count is not.
push_opt_out — new, alongside the existing push_subscribe. Reminder opt-out rate by path is one of the four numbers the research says to instrument first, and it is the tripwire on the reminder copy.
audio_play — existing, keep. Detail should carry whether it was the hero or a plan card, to answer "audio toggle usage" (research, Persona 3 tests).
plan_start / plan_complete — existing, keep. Add days_elapsed on complete, so we finally learn the completion rate for a year-long plan, which the research says exists nowhere.

Rollups needed (one nightly job over the existing activity table): D1/D7/D30 by persona; median days_read in a rolling 7 by persona; drawer-open rate; median seconds_on_passage with the drawer opened vs not; catch-up rebase rate and its 30-day retention delta. Every one of these is a persona-segmented cut of events that already have a pipeline (analytics.ts → track-activity → analytics-dashboard.js) — the work is the allowlist, the segment and the rollup, not new infrastructure.
self_serve_levers: Campus study note, no developer: a campus pastor publishes through the existing staff intake form at /staff. corner_add already accepts a typed item and CORNER_TYPES already includes "note" (netlify/functions/lib/intake-core.js:40, 295-303), publishing to campus_content. One additive change makes it land in the Study drawer: a nullable ref column on campus_content and an optional ref on the corner_add item. After that migration ships, a pastor writes a note on Genesis 12 and it appears in their campus's readers' Study drawer as "From Alpharetta · Ryan" with no deploy.

The intake form itself is data, not code: question_save, question_delete and question_reorder (netlify/functions/intake.js:721-756) mean the questions a campus pastor answers can be added or reworded without a release. If Ashley wants campuses supplying weekly study notes, that is a new question row, not a build.
Removing a published note is equally self-serve: corner_remove (intake-core.js:288-293) already deletes by id, scoped to the pastor's own campus.
Reader-level, no developer at all: reminder on/off and reminder hour in MoreScreen; translation; Compare translation; path change through the sheet from four doors; campus through the header chip.

Honest limits — these stay developer-only after this build, and should be named as such rather than promised: the plan catalogue (src/data/plans.ts, and a plan id is referenced in four places that must all be rewired); the curated commentary set (src/data/commentary.ts); push notification templates and the 40-passage fallback rotation (netlify/functions/push-send.js); the featured-three plan list (persona-config.ts:17). If self-serve control of the featured three matters, the smallest honest path is to read them from a campus_content row rather than to build an admin screen.

open_decisions: "Read with" one person — the research calls it the one social feature the Pew decline argues for (weekly Bible-study group participation fell 24% → 13%, 2014-2025) and your own research doc lists the decision as yours: day-count only, or nothing at all. It is not in this two-week build either way; it needs your word before it is designed.

The rhythm floor: does a week count as kept at 4 days read out of 7, or 5? This sets what "12 weeks running" means and it cannot be changed later without invalidating everyone's number, so it is worth deciding once, now.

Is "Move the plan to today" allowed on Through the Bible in a Year, or must a year plan stay calendar-true? Rebasing is the grace mechanic, but it means the reader finishes the Bible in 365 reading days rather than 365 calendar days. My recommendation is yes, allow it, and say so in the copy — but it is a plan-integrity call, not a design one.

Chronological is the plan the research names first for this persona and the catalogue does not have one. Adding it is a data addition to plans.ts, but a new plan id is referenced in four places (personalization.ts, SetupPromptModal.tsx, PlansScreen.tsx, PastorStudyOnboarding.tsx) and all four must be rewired. Build it, or leave the three we have?

Once the six named commentaries are wired in, does AI Insight stay as the last-resort tab for chapters with no published note, or is it dropped for this persona? It is labelled honestly either way; the question is whether you want an AI paragraph next to Calvin.

"Read like paper" — larger type, no chrome — is a real research finding for this persona (89% of Bible users still prefer print) and it is not in this two-week build. Worth doing later, or not at all?
risks: This is a reshape of the opening screen for one persona, which is the exact class of change that was rejected on 1 Sep. It ships behind a deploy preview, it is not merged without your word, and the preview link is the deliverable — not the merge.

Collapsing commentary can read as "stripped", which is the specific complaint that killed the last opening-screen change. The mitigation is structural: nothing leaves the screen. Commentary keeps a source line and a two-line preview; Compare and Greek & Hebrew are promoted from chrome into a visible, named Study row. The screen gets richer in labelling and quieter in noise. If the preview still reads thin, the fallback is to keep commentary's first paragraph rather than two lines — a one-value change, not a rebuild.

Completion numbers will drop the week this ships, because handleRead stops crediting the plan day on chapter expand. That drop is the fix working, not a regression. It must be written into the PR description or it will be read as a bug in a fortnight.

dw_read_days is a new synced key. Done wrong it either resurrects deleted days or wipes a second device's history. It follows the highlights union-merge pattern exactly (cloudSync.ts:320-335): merge the set of date strings, never replace, and never rebuild it from React state.

Rebasing a plan's startedAt writes to dw_activeplans, which merges across devices. It must read the record fresh from localStorage and touch only that plan's startedAt, or a second device's completed days are overwritten by stale mount-time state.
The reminder change cannot be verified on a deploy preview — pushSupported() allowlists only prod, www and localhost. It is proven on localhost before merge and re-checked on prod after.

streak.ts is shared by all five personas. The rhythm counter is a separate module read only by the deeper_study greeting; streak.ts is not modified. If it were, every other path's greeting and milestone behaviour would move at the same time.
New CSS uses the dw-st-* prefix. dw-path-* is taken by the Plans-tab chooser and dw-cp-* by the path sheet; dw-st-* and dw-study-* currently have zero occurrences in src/, so the prefix is clean.

If any plan JSON or /books content changes as part of this, /books/* must stay network-first with cache as offline fallback, and CACHE_NAME, STATIC_CACHE and SW_VERSION are bumped together — otherwise returning readers never see the change.
